title: U.S. House · Washington's 3rd District
area: Southwest Washington, including Vancouver, Clark, Cowlitz, Lewis, Pacific, Skamania and Wahkiakum counties.

context.text: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez and John Braun advanced from the August 4, 2026 top-two primary. Perez and three other Democrats combined for 55.9% of the primary vote; Braun and two other Republicans combined for 42.0%. Perez was first elected in 2022, defeating Joe Kent 50.1%-49.3%, and won re-election in 2024 by 51.7%-47.9% over Kent. Donald Trump carried the district 50.3%-47.0% in 2024, making it one of the U.S. House districts Democrats are defending that Trump won. Ballotpedia identified this race as a 2026 battleground.

Brent Hennrich, a Democrat who placed third in the primary with 15.3% of the vote, said he would not support Perez in the general election, telling the Washington State Standard: "I want [Perez] out of office ... I've told my supporters what I'm doing and I've told them to vote their conscience."
As of July 15, 2026, Perez had raised $6.29 million to Braun's $2.04 million.

candidates.name: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4 top-two primary as part of a combined 55.9% Democratic vote share

summary.text: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Washington's 3rd District, first elected in 2022. She is a small-business owner who sits on the House Committee on Appropriations.

background.text: Born in Harris County, Texas; lives in Skamania County, Washington. Earned a bachelor's degree in economics from Reed College in 2012.
Founded and owns an auto repair shop in Washington's 3rd District before being elected to Congress.

priorities.text: Says she is "fighting to ensure every woman can see a doctor whenever she wants, for whatever reason" and will work to prevent a national abortion ban.
priorities.quote: Marie is fighting to ensure every woman can see a doctor whenever she wants, for whatever reason. Because that is her right, and once freedom is limited, it's lost.

priorities.text: Highlights right-to-repair legislation to stop farm and consumer equipment manufacturers from requiring customers to pay the original manufacturer for repairs, drawing on her experience running an auto repair shop.
Says she is working to bring down housing costs, increase childcare options, and expand the Child Tax Credit for working families.
Cites securing $600 million in federal funding toward replacing the I-5 bridge as a down payment on infrastructure for Southwest Washington.

positions.summary: Supports legal access to abortion and says she will work to prevent a national abortion ban.
positions.quote: Marie is fighting to ensure every woman can see a doctor whenever she wants, for whatever reason.

positions.summary: States that climate change is real and man-made and disproportionately affects the working class; has backed tax rebates for energy-efficiency upgrades.
Campaign platform emphasizes lowering healthcare costs and cutting out middlemen rather than a specific public-coverage expansion.
Supports re-introducing and expanding the Child Tax Credit and increasing childcare accessibility, particularly in rural communities.
Campaign platform lists increased border security as part of her approach to the drug crisis, alongside expanded treatment and rehab access.

record.text: Sits on the House Committee on Appropriations for the 2025-2026 Congress, on the Agriculture-Rural Development-FDA and Financial Services-General Government subcommittees.
In the 2023-2024 Congress, served on the Committee on Agriculture and the Committee on Small Business, where she was ranking member of the Rural Development, Energy, and Supply Chains subcommittee.

candidates.name: John Braun
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the August 4 top-two primary as part of a combined 42.0% Republican vote share

summary.text: John Braun is a Republican state senator representing Washington's 20th Legislative District since 2013 and a manufacturing executive running for the U.S. House seat held by Marie Gluesenkamp Perez.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Navy and Navy Reserve for 31 years, including service in the submarine force.
Earned a B.S. in electrical engineering from the University of Washington in 1989 and an M.S. in manufacturing engineering and an MBA from the University of Michigan in 1999.
President of Braun Northwest, an emergency vehicle manufacturer based in Chehalis with about 350 employees.

priorities.text: Says he will "complete high-priority barriers, hire and equip more agents, deploy proven technology, tighten asylum loopholes, and go after cartel supply chains" on border security, and notes he opposed a 2023 state rifle ban.
priorities.quote: I entered this race focused on border security and the fentanyl crisis. I'll complete high-priority barriers, hire and equip more agents, deploy proven technology, tighten asylum loopholes, and go after cartel supply chains.

priorities.text: On energy, supports market-based production including hydropower, solar, oil, natural gas and nuclear power to meet rising demand from AI data centers.
Authored the state College Affordability Program, which he describes as the largest cuts to public university tuition in the nation, and supports expanding skilled-trades training.
Supports the federal Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act and says he would vote to base women's sports eligibility on biological sex.

positions.summary: Supports completing border barriers, hiring more agents, tightening asylum loopholes, and targeting cartel supply chains; says his opponent (in a 2023 state legislative vote) voted against the federal Secure the Border Act.
Opposed Washington's 2023 state rifle ban and says he will protect the constitutional rights of gun owners and sportsmen in Congress.
Supports an "all of the above" energy approach including hydropower, solar, oil, natural gas and nuclear power rather than a transition away from fossil fuels specifically.
Supports the federal Parents Bill of Rights and says parents, not "bureaucrats," should control decisions about their children's education.

record.text: Has represented Washington's 20th Legislative District in the state Senate since 2013.
Says he authored Washington's College Affordability Program as a state senator, which he describes as cutting public university tuition.
